hero.title: Different agents. Deterministic workflow. Consistent delivery.
hero.lede: AI agents can generate code. Delivery requires something harder: preserving intent, evidence and decision quality as work moves across roles, sessions, candidates and release gates. This page renders live from data/sessions/ -- one record per merged pull request, contributed automatically by whichever harness did the work -- instead of hand-authored retrospective prose.
hero.claim: Agents reason. AgentFlow makes delivery repeatable.

narrative.spine: An agent can interpret incomplete information and propose a course of action. AgentFlow validates whether that proposal belongs to the current goal, role, candidate and gate. A passing test does not prove deployment. A tag does not prove public behavior. An agent’s confidence does not advance a gate. Every transition needs evidence appropriate to that decision.
narrative.boundaries: This delivery was predominantly single-agent and multi-role. Fresh-context advisors were same-platform processes, not independent human reviewers. Local checks do not prove GitHub state; GitHub checks do not prove a release; a release does not prove the hosted application changed. AgentFlow did not write the application by itself. Agents and tools produced observations; AgentFlow governed how those observations became durable delivery decisions.
narrative.closing: AwesomeAwesomeness is the shipped case. AgentFlow is the reason its delivery can be reconstructed. Start with any session below and follow it back to the issue, manifest, pull request, or evidence that supports it.
